title: Resilience risk profile and handoff log - Nov 12 2026
body:
Weekly snapshot (2026-11-06 -> 2026-11-12)

Summary:
- Primary focus: reduce risk for cache stampede under high prefix-sharing workloads and complete runbook dry-run for the model routing fallback sequence.
- This doc captures: incident summaries, current SLO health, results from the runbook dry-run, proactive mitigations and a concise on-call handoff for the coming week.

Incident highlights (not full postmortems):
1) INC-2026-1121 — downstream redis cluster latency spike (2026-11-09 02:14 UTC)
   - Symptom: P99 request latency for inference gateway increased from 380ms -> 1.8s for ~18 minutes.
   - Root cause (triage): transient multi-AZ network flapping impacted one Redis read replica used for prefix KV lookups; fallback to local in-memory cache worked but cache-warmup caused a spike.
   - Impact: small number (~0.6%) of requests hit degraded tail latency; business metrics unaffected.
   - Containment: failover to primary, demoted problematic replica; rolling restart and network team notified.
   - Follow-ups: revisit replica health checks and add increased weighting for local cache before remote read on high-QPS endpoints. Ticket: INC-2026-1121.

2) INC-2026-1108 — canary rollout mismatch (2026-11-07 11:40 UTC)
   - Symptom: canary traffic routed to model variant v2.1 which had an unexpected tokenization edge-case for emojis.
   - Impact: ~2% of canary requests returned malformed structured outputs; auto-fallback worked but increased token cost.
   - Root cause: canary rollout config omitted tokenizer compatibility check in pipeline.
   - Mitigation: paused rollout, reverted routing rule.
   - Follow-ups: add tokenizer compat check to canary preflight (OPS-7845).

3) Minor flipper alerts (multiple short-lived alerts)
   - Aged alert noise: non-actionable metrics from an old exporter; reduced signal-to-noise after removing exporter metric namespace.

SLO snapshot (as of 2026-11-12 06:00 UTC):
- Inference API availability (global): 99.95% (30-day window) vs goal 99.99%
  - Error budget remaining (30d): 17%. Trend: slow erosion over last 3 weeks due to small tail incidents and increased background maintenance.
- P95 latency (text-gen): 260ms (goal 220ms) — note: increased client-side batching and longer sequences influenced this.
- P99 latency (text-gen): 1.2s (goal 750ms) — driven by cache-warmups and occasional GC pauses on dedicated hosts.
- Action: prioritize two workstreams this sprint: cache warmup strategies (pre-warming on scale events) and investigate GC tuning for a subset of dedicated host pools.

Runbook dry-run (2026-11-11):
- Objective: exercise model routing fallback path and on-call coordination for a simulated multi-failure (KV store + routing controller).
- Participants: Jordan Patel (lead), Maya Lin (routing), Diego Alvarez (KV stub), Priya Nair (observer).
- What we did: triggered the simulated KV-latency and then induced the routing controller to re-route to fallback model tier.
- Observations:
  - Handover messaging worked (Slack bridge + pager); some friction in documenting exact rollback commands in the routing CLI.
  - Timing: full fallback path executed in ~2m 40s. Manual steps took ~1m 15s; routing CLI options unclear to first-time user.
  - Failure mode not covered: partial fallback where only some regions switch while others remain on primary — we need a safer partial-rollout check.
- Outcomes / changes to runbook:
  - Add a short QuickStart subsection with exact CLI commands and example flags.
  - Add a checklist item to verify region convergence (heatmap check) before marking incident resolved.
  - Create a one-click script to perform the fallback in <= 90s (PR created: infra#314).

Proactive mitigations & recommended priorities:
- Cache warmup and soft-limits:
  - Implement gradual prefix-based pre-warm on scale events (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-11-26).
  - Add per-prefix request counters to detect hot-prefix emergence and auto-increase local cache retention (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-11-19).
- Routing safety:
  - Add tokenizer compatibility preflight to canary pipeline (owner: Maya Lin, ticket OPS-7845, due: 2026-11-20).
  - Add a region-convergence assertion into rollout automation (owner: Jordan Patel, due: 2026-11-22).
- Observability tweaks:
  - Add a new metric: fallback-rate-by-region. Include in SRE dashboard (owner: Jordan Patel, due: 2026-11-18).
  - Reduce alert noise by filtering legacy exporter namespaces (owner: Platform telemetry, due: 2026-11-15).

On-call handoff (next on-call: 2026-11-13 -> 2026-11-20)
- Known issues to watch:
  - INC-2026-1121 follow-up: replica health check patch rolling (monitor for repeated latency spikes).
  - Runbook changes in flight: fallback script (infra#314) — validate in staging before merging.
  - Upcoming maintenance window 2026-11-16 02:00-03:00 UTC for a minor router upgrade (expected brief 10s connection drops).
- Paging thresholds and escalation notes:
  - Keep existing P99 latency alert thresholds but add a suppression window during the maintenance window. Confirm with Pager duty (action: Jordan).
  - Escalation path unchanged: on-call -> senior on-call -> SRE lead (Slack #sre-urgent and PagerDuty).
- Contacts for this handoff:
  - Jordan Patel (lead) — pager on Slack and PD
  - Maya Lin (routing) — Slack @mayalin
  - Diego Alvarez (platform infra) — on-call mobile

Open action items (tracked owners & due dates):
- Diego: implement cache pre-warm prototype (due 2026-11-26)
- Priya: instrument per-prefix counters + dashboard (due 2026-11-19)
- Maya: add tokenizer preflight to canary (OPS-7845) (due 2026-11-20)
- Jordan: add region convergence check into rollout automation + dashboard tile (due 2026-11-22)
- Platform telemetry: remove legacy exporter metrics (due 2026-11-15)

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working doc; iterative updates expected as we complete the runbook PR and follow-up fixes. Please add comments inline or ping on Slack thread #sre-weekly.

Quick reference (commands and links):
- Routing fallback CLI example: routingctl fallback --model-tier fallback-v1 --converge-check
- Runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Cache+Stampede+Mitigation+Playbook
- PR for one-click fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/314

End of note.
